description: Named Balaka and presented as the first aircraft of Bangladesh; photographed on display at the museum in 2014 2016 and 2016; note the museum's own signage confusion — a Wikipedia summary calls it a 1958 Russian passenger aircraft which does not fit an An-24PB
aliases: An24; An-24; An-24PB; Coke; Balaka; An24PB

description: The Dakota used in the 1971 Liberation War; the BAF's Kilo Flight improvised it as a bomber; no serial recorded in the sources I reached
aliases: C47; C-47; DC-3; DC3; Dakota; Skytrain

description: The Kilo Flight Otter used in operations against Chittagong seaport during the 1971 Liberation War; the museum nameplate photographed in 2016 renders the type as "Airtech Canadian DH 3/1000" which is a garbled transcription of DHC-3 Otter
aliases: DHC3; DHC-3; Otter; DH-3; DH3

description: Indian Air Force Hunter used in support of Bangladesh during the 1971 Liberation War and later gifted by the IAF to the Bangladesh Air Force; no serial recorded
aliases: Hunter; Hawker Hunter

description: Indian Air Force Chetak — the Indian licence-built Aerospatiale Alouette III — added to the museum in December 2016 per a dated first-hand photograph; Chetaks flew gunship escort for the Sylhet heliborne assault in December 1971
aliases: Chetak; SA 316; SA316; Alouette III; Z-1829

description: Indian Air Force Mi-4; Mi-4s carried out the heliborne infantry assault near Sylhet on 7 December 1971; flown into Bangladesh aboard an IAF C-17 and formally handed over before being moved to the museum; photographed in place in May 2018
aliases: Mi4; Mi-4; Hound; Z-2401

description: Described on site as the first VIP helicopter of Bangladesh obtained from Russia in 1972; no serial recorded
aliases: Mi8; Mi-8; Hip

description: Photographed at the museum in 2014
aliases: MiG21; MiG-21MF; MiG21MF; Fishbed

description: Photographed at the museum in 2015 2017 and 2018; the 2018 photographer noted it had been repainted into correct markings
aliases: MiG21; MiG-21MF; MiG21MF; Fishbed

description: Two-seat trainer photographed inside BAF Base Bashar in 2014 and photographed being placed at the museum in July 2015; the move is documented
aliases: MiG21; MiG-21UM; MiG21UM; Mongol; Mongol-B

description: Chinese-built two-seat trainer development of the MiG-17 built by Shenyang Aircraft Corporation; construction number 551723; first flew for the BAF on 3 June 1979 and last flew on 1 January 1985; four are said to have served — 723 724 725 and 506
aliases: FT5; FT-5; JJ-5; JJ5; MiG-17U; MiG17U; c/n 551723

description: Chinese-built derivative of the MiG-19 built by Shenyang Aircraft Corporation; photographed at the museum; no serial legible
aliases: F6; F-6; J-6; J6; MiG-19; MiG19; Farmer

description: Chinese-built two-seat trainer development of the MiG-19; photographed at the museum in 2016; no serial legible
aliases: FT6; FT-6; JJ-6; JJ6; MiG-19UTI; Farmer; MiG19UTI

description: Export A-5III built by Nanchang Aircraft Manufacturing Corporation; photographed at the museum in 2016 and 2023 with the marking A-5111 which combines the type designation and the airframe number; recorded as A-5111 exactly as worn
aliases: Q5; Q-5; A-5; A5; A-5III; A5III; Fantan; A-5111A; Q5III

description: Ex-Pakistan Air Force airframe taken over by Bangladesh; photographed at the museum in January 2016; one of two ex-PAF Sabres preserved in Bangladesh — the other is 1606 at BAF Base Zahurul Haque
aliases: CL13; CL-13; Sabre 6; Sabre Mk 6; F-86; F86

description: Recorded in Wikipedia's surviving-Gnat register as a HAL Ajeet — the Indian licence-developed Gnat — at the Bangladesh Air Force Museum; photographed as a Gnat at the museum in 2016; operator recorded as India because the Ajeet served only with the Indian Air Force
aliases: Gnat; Ajeet; HAL Ajeet

description: French-built 1960 airframe; the museum states it was inducted into the Bangladesh Air Force in 1997; photographed as a museum exhibit and noted in 2017 as originally a BAF Museum aircraft
aliases: CM170; CM.170; CM-170; Magister; Fouga Magister

description: Photographed at the museum in 2016; no serial legible and the sub-variant is not recorded
aliases: T37; T-37; Tweet; Tweety Bird

description: New Zealand-built Airtourer; the museum states it joined the Bangladesh Air Force in 1997; the design originated with Victa in Australia and production moved to Aero Engine Services Ltd in New Zealand
aliases: Airtourer; Victa Airtourer; AESL Airtourer; CT-4; CT4

description: Chinese-built primary trainer displayed under its export designation PT-6; the museum states it arrived in 1985
aliases: CJ6; CJ-6; PT-6; PT6; Nanchang CJ-6

description: Gifted by Germany for Bangladesh Air Force gliding experience and brought to Bangladesh in 1982; type not identified on any source I reached and deliberately not guessed
aliases: Glider; Segelflugzeug
